newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open in doldrums, demand muted.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open in doldrums, demand muted.

text.p: Singapore shares were becalmed in the doldrums early on Tuesday as institutional demand remained slight in a market lacking direction, dealers said.
Interest in blue chip stocks remained poor, with funds still switching out of low yield counters, dampening sentiment.
Retail buyers, however, nibbled on newly-listed initial public offerings which continued to provide upward momentum for issues like Raffles Medical Group and Australand Holdings.
The Straits Times Industrials Index eased 3.05 points to 1,988.03 at 0220 GMT on a thin volume of 23 million lots.
But advancing issues beat decliners 87 to 47.
Dealers said investors were not urgent about buying ahead of the Singapore budget, expected to be discussed by parliament soon, and interim results in August.
"There is the budget stalling trade, and interims, which could spell more bad corporate results," a local dealer said.

Most traded was DBS Land, but it remained unchanged at Singapore $4.72, underpinned by good demand for newly-listed unit Australand. That stock rose six Australian cents to A$1.51, catching up with values seen in Australia, where it is also listed.
